translation_en: Ibn Salam narrated to us: Hushaim informed us, from Husayn, from Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father, concerning when they slept through the prayer. The Prophet said, “Allah took your souls when He willed and returned them when He willed.” They attended to their needs and performed ablution until the sun had risen and become bright, then he stood and prayed.

Yahya ibn Qaza‘ah narrated to us: Ibrahim narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Salamah and al-A‘raj. Ismail narrated to us: My brother narrated to me, from Sulayman, from Muhammad ibn Abi Atiq, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman and Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, that Abu Hurayrah said: A Muslim man and a Jewish man exchanged insults. The Muslim swore, “By the One who chose Muhammad above all people,” and the Jew swore, “By the One who chose Moses above all people.” The Muslim raised his hand and slapped the Jew. The Jew went to the Messenger of Allah and told him what had happened between them. The Prophet said, “Do not give me precedence over Moses, for people will be struck unconscious on the Day of Resurrection, and I will be the first to recover. Then I will see Moses holding on to the side of the Throne. I do not know whether he was among those who were struck unconscious and recovered before me, or among those whom Allah exempted.”

Ishaq ibn Abi Isa informed us: Yazid ibn Harun informed us: Shu‘bah informed us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah said, “The Dajjal will come to Medina and find angels guarding it, so the Dajjal will not approach it, nor will the plague, if Allah wills.”

Abu al-Yaman informed us: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri: Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to me that Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah said, “Every Prophet had a supplication. If Allah wills, I wish to reserve my supplication as intercession for my community on the Day of Resurrection.”

Yasrah ibn Safwan ibn Jamil al-Lakhmi narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said, “While I was sleeping, I saw myself at a well and drew from it as much as Allah willed. Then Ibn Abi Quhafah took the bucket and drew one or two buckets, and there was weakness in his drawing—may Allah forgive him. Then Umar took it, and it became a large bucket. I never saw a masterful person among the people draw as he did, until the people watered their camels and rested them at the watering place.”

Muhammad ibn al-Ala narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Burayd, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, who said: When a petitioner—or a person with a need—came to the Prophet, he would say, “Intercede, and you will be rewarded; Allah will decree whatever He wills through the tongue of His Messenger.”

Yahya narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from Ma‘mar, from Hammam, who heard Abu Hurayrah narrate from the Prophet, who said, “None of you should say, ‘O Allah, forgive me if You will; have mercy on me if You will; provide for me if You will.’ Let him be firm in asking, for He does whatever He wills and no one can compel Him.”

Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Abu Hafs, Amr, narrated to us: al-Awza‘i narrated to us: Ibn Shihab narrated to me, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah ibn Mas‘ud, from Ibn Abbas, who said: He and al-Hurr ibn Qays ibn Hisn al-Fazari disagreed about Moses’ companion, whether he was Khadir. Ubayy ibn Ka‘b al-Ansari passed by them, so Ibn Abbas called him and said, “My companion and I disagree about Moses’ companion, whom he sought a way to meet. Have you heard the Messenger of Allah mention his story?” He said, “Yes. I heard the Messenger of Allah say: While Moses was among an assembly of the Children of Israel, a man came and asked, ‘Do you know anyone more learned than you?’ Moses said, ‘No.’ Allah revealed to Moses, ‘Yes, Our servant Khadir is.’ Moses asked for a way to meet him. Allah made the fish a sign for him and told him, ‘When you lose the fish, turn back, for you will meet him.’ Moses followed the fish’s tracks through the sea. Moses’ young companion said to him, ‘Do you remember when we took refuge at the rock? I forgot the fish, and none but Satan made me forget to mention it.’ Moses said, ‘That is what we were seeking.’ So they retraced their steps and found Khadir. The rest of their story was as Allah narrated.”

Abu al-Yaman informed us: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri. Ahmad ibn Salih said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah, who said, “Tomorrow, if Allah wills, we will camp at Khayf Banu Kinana, where they swore an oath of disbelief.” He meant al-Muhassab.

Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Amr, from Abu al-Abbas, from Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: The Prophet besieged the people of Taif but did not conquer it. He said, “We are departing, if Allah wills.” The Muslims said, “We are departing without having conquered it.” He said, “Then go out to fight tomorrow.” They went out the next morning and were wounded. The Prophet said, “We are departing tomorrow, if Allah wills.” This seemed to please them, and the Messenger of Allah smiled.

Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Amr, from Ikrimah, from Abu Hurayrah, who attributed it to the Prophet: “When Allah decrees a matter in heaven, the angels beat their wings in submission to His words, as though it were a chain dragged over smooth stone”—Ali said, “Another narrator said: over stone”—“and it passes through them. When terror is removed from their hearts, they say, ‘What did your Lord say?’ They say, ‘The truth; He is the Most High, the Great.’” Ali said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Amr, from Ikrimah, from Abu Hurayrah, with this report. Sufyan said: Amr said, “I heard Ikrimah narrate to us: Abu Hurayrah narrated to us.” Ali said: I asked Sufyan, “Did he say, ‘I heard Ikrimah say, I heard Abu Hurayrah’?” He said, “Yes.” I said to Sufyan, “Someone narrated from Amr, from Ikrimah, from Abu Hurayrah, attributing it to the Prophet, that he recited ‘fuzzi‘a’.” Sufyan said, “That is how Amr recited it; I do not know whether he heard it that way or not.” Sufyan said, “That is our recitation.”

Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us, from Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab: Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman informed me, from Abu Hurayrah, who used to say that the Messenger of Allah said, “Allah has not listened to anything as He listens to a Prophet who recites the Quran aloud.” A companion of his said: He means that the Prophet recites it aloud.

Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us: My father narrated to us: al-A‘mash narrated to us: Abu Salih narrated to us, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, who said: The Prophet said, “Allah will say, ‘O Adam.’ He will reply, ‘At Your service and at Your pleasure.’ Then a voice will call out: Allah commands you to send forth a contingent from your descendants to the Fire.”

Ubayd ibn Ismail narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from Aishah, who said: I was not jealous of any woman as I was jealous of Khadijah, for his Lord had commanded him to give her the glad tidings of a house in Paradise.

Ishaq narrated to me: Abd al-Samad narrated to us: Abd al-Rahman—Ibn Abdullah ibn Dinar—narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said, “When Allah, Blessed and Exalted, loves a servant, He calls Gabriel: ‘Allah loves so-and-so, so love him.’ Gabriel loves him. Then Gabriel calls out in heaven, ‘Allah loves so-and-so, so love him,’ and the inhabitants of heaven love him, and acceptance of him is placed among the people of earth.”

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us, from Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said, “Angels take turns among you by night and by day, and they gather at the Asr and dawn prayers. Then those who spent the night among you ascend, and He asks them, though He knows best, ‘How did you leave My servants?’ They say, ‘We left them while they were praying, and we came to them while they were praying.’”

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Ghundar narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Wasıl, from al-Ma‘rur, who said: I heard Abu Dharr narrate from the Prophet, who said, “Gabriel came to me and gave me the glad tidings that whoever dies without associating anything with Allah will enter Paradise.” I said, “Even if he stole and committed adultery?” He said, “Even if he stole and committed adultery.”

Musaddad narrated to us: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us: Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani narrated to us, from al-Bara ibn Azib, who said: The Messenger of Allah said, “O so-and-so, when you go to your bed, say: O Allah, I surrender myself to You, turn my face to You, entrust my affair to You, and rely upon You, in hope and fear of You. There is no refuge or escape from You except with You. I believe in Your Book which You sent down and in Your Prophet whom You sent.” If you die that night, you will die upon the natural way; and if you wake in the morning, you will have attained reward.

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ismail ibn Abi Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa, who said: On the Day of the Confederates, the Messenger of Allah said, “O Allah, Revealer of the Book, swift in reckoning, defeat the confederates and shake them.” Al-Humaydi added: Sufyan narrated to us: Ibn Abi Khalid narrated to us: I heard Abdullah say: I heard the Prophet.

Musaddad narrated to us, from Hushaym, from Abu Bishr, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding “Do not recite your prayer aloud, nor recite it silently” Quran 17:110. He said: It was revealed while the Messenger of Allah was concealed in Mecca. When he raised his voice, the polytheists heard him and reviled the Quran, the One who sent it down, and the one who brought it. Allah Most High said, “Do not recite your prayer aloud, nor recite it silently”: do not recite it aloud so the polytheists hear, and do not recite it so quietly that your companions cannot hear you. “Seek a way between that” Quran 17:110: let them hear you, but do not recite so loudly that they take the Quran from you.

Al-Humaydi narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us: al-Zuhri narrated to us, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet said, “Allah Most High says, ‘The son of Adam offends Me: he curses time, while I am Time. The matter is in My hand; I turn night and day.’”

Abu Nu‘aym narrated to us: al-A‘mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said: “Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says, ‘Fasting is for Me, and I reward it. He gives up his desire, food, and drink for My sake. Fasting is a shield. The fasting person has two joys: joy when he breaks his fast and joy when he meets his Lord. The smell from the mouth of a fasting person is more pleasant to Allah than the fragrance of musk.’”

Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma‘mar informed us, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said, “While Ayyub was bathing naked, a swarm of golden locusts fell upon him, and he began gathering them into his garment. His Lord called to him, ‘O Ayyub, have I not made you independent of what you see?’ He replied, ‘Indeed, by Your might, my Lord, but I cannot do without Your blessing.’”

Ismail narrated to us: Malik narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Abdullah al-Agharr, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said, “Our Lord, Blessed and Exalted, descends every night to the lowest heaven when the final third of the night remains and says, ‘Who is calling upon Me, that I may answer him? Who is asking Me, that I may give him? Who is seeking My forgiveness, that I may forgive him?’”

Abu al-Yaman informed us: Shu‘ayb informed us: Abu al-Zinad narrated to us, that al-A‘raj narrated to him, that he heard Abu Hurayrah say that he heard the Messenger of Allah say, “We are the last, yet we will be the foremost on the Day of Resurrection.” With this same chain: “Allah says, ‘Spend, and I will spend on you.’”

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Umārah, from Abu Zur‘ah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: Gabriel said, “This is Khadijah. She has come to you with a vessel containing food or drink. Convey to her greetings of peace from her Lord and give her the glad tidings of a house of reeds in which there will be neither clamour nor weariness.”

Muadh ibn Asad informed us: Abdullah informed us: Ma‘mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said: “Allah said, ‘I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and what has never occurred to a human heart.’”

Mahmud narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj informed us: Sulayman al-Ahwal informed me that Tawus informed him that he heard Ibn Abbas say: When the Prophet prayed at night, he would say, “O Allah, praise belongs to You. You are the Light of the heavens and earth, You sustain the heavens and earth, and You are the Lord of the heavens and earth and all in them. You are the Truth; Your promise, word, and meeting You are true; Paradise, the Fire, the Prophets, and the Hour are true. O Allah, to You I submit, in You I believe, upon You I rely, to You I turn, by You I contend, and to You I refer judgment. Forgive what I sent ahead and left behind, what I concealed and declared. You are my God; there is no god but You.”

Hajjaj ibn Minhal narrated to us: Abdullah ibn Umar al-Numayri narrated to us: Yunus ibn Yazid al-Ayli narrated to us: I heard al-Zuhri say: I heard Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, Alqamah ibn Waqqas, and Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah narrate about the report of Aishah, the wife of the Prophet, concerning what the people of the slander said about her and how Allah declared her innocent of it. Each of them narrated to me part of what he had heard from Aishah. She said: By Allah, I never thought that Allah would send down recited revelation declaring me innocent. I considered my situation too insignificant for Allah to speak about me in a matter that would be recited. I only hoped that the Messenger of Allah might see a dream in which Allah would declare me innocent. Then Allah Most High revealed, “Indeed, those who brought the slander…” the ten verses Quran 24:11.

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: al-Mughirah ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said: “Allah says, ‘When My servant intends to do a bad deed, do not record it against him until he does it. If he does it, record it as one like it. If he leaves it for My sake, record it for him as a good deed. When he intends to do a good deed but does not do it, record it for him as a good deed. If he does it, record it for him as ten times its like, up to seven hundred times.’”
